name: CA-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 13 points and Carbajal is a sitting incumbent
Carbajal holds a roughly ten-to-one cash advantage ($3.5M vs. $81K on hand)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98 percent
No public polling or outside spending signals a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's D+13 lean, Carbajal's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge all point the same direction, and prediction markets price his win odds near 98 percent. With no polling or outside spending suggesting competition, the forecast stays at a large Democratic margin.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending on Smith's behalf or polling showing a far tighter race would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 24th District leans Democratic by about 13 points, and incumbent Salud Carbajal is seeking re-election against Republican Bob Smith. Carbajal holds a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $1.9 million and entering the general election with $3.5 million on hand, while Smith has raised about $329,000 with $81,000 available. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race on either side.

Prediction markets give Carbajal roughly a 98 percent chance of winning, and no public general-election polls or expert ratings contest that picture. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes Smith a clear underdog who would need an external shock to close the margin. The main uncertainty comes from the absence of recent polling rather than any evidence of a competitive race.
